annotations.text: Settings joins the landing column itself. The ship stop already taught the column the grammar this needs: a stop can open a panel at the column's own width. So settings becomes a stop and the corner MENU key disappears from the home screen entirely.

At rest: the settings stop rides at the head of the column, above the account, shorter and dimmer than the three below it. Present and findable, but visibly not part of the sentence that ends in PLAY NOW.

Open: the panel climbs from the stop the way the ship pager climbs from the ship stop. Everything the drawer's settings page held is here, banded the same way, with Controls and About opening in place.

The alternative that costs no stop: a quiet mono line under PLAY NOW opening the same panel. Cheapest presence, but it puts the way to turn the music down in the smallest type on the screen, and a first session will not find it.

The landing exists only in the stands, so the drawer's death leaves a seated pilot needing exactly three things: the way out of the seat, which side it is on, and the volume. The corner key keeps the mixer icon mid-match and opens only that. Everything else waits at home.
